entries.title: Isaiah 30:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 The prophet threatens the people for their confidence in Egypt, 8 and contempt of God's word. 18 God's mercies towards his church. 27 God's wrath and the people's joy, in the destruction of Assyria.

A.M. cir. 3291. entries.title: Isaiah 30:28
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
his breath. 11:4; Ps 18:15; Lu 22:31; 2Th 2:8; Heb 4:12; Re 1:16; 2:16 an overflowing. 8:8; 28:17,18; 29:6; Hab 3:12-15 to sift.Bp. Lowth renders, "to toss the nations with the van of perdition;" that is, says {Kimchi,} nothing useful shall remain behind, but all shall come to nothing and perish. The van of the ancients was a large instrument, somewhat like a shovel, with a long handle, with which they tossed the corn mixed with the chaff and chopped straw into the air, that the wind might separate them.

19:12,14; 33:10-12; Ho 13:3; Am 9:9; Mt 3:12 a bridle. 37:29; 2Ki 19:28; Ps 32:9; Pr 26:3 causing. 19:3,13,14; 2Sa 17:14; 1Ki 22:20-22; Job 39:17; Eze 14:7-9 2Th 2:11
